transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to the clinic? What's been going on that made you decide to seek help?

Hi. Thank you for seeing me, I really appreciate it. Um... I guess my mom is the one who wanted me to come, mostly. I hope it's okay that I'm here. 

It's just... I don't want to sound lazy, I'm really trying, but lately I mostly just can't make myself do anything anymore. I used to do a lot of things, like knitting and journaling, and I'd go out for walks, but now I just kind of sit in my room all day. It's actually really embarrassing to say, please don't think badly of me, but I've kind of just been sitting there in the same clothes. I just don't have the energy to change them. Even when my mom comes in and asks what's wrong, I... I barely have the energy to answer her. 

I feel awful for worrying her. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it right.
How long have you been feeling this way—not having energy to do things and sitting in your room? Can you remember when this started?

Um... I guess it's been... well, a little while. I really hope it doesn't make me sound terrible, but... I think this whole thing kind of started when I enrolled in a community-college program. That was... gosh, about two years and two months ago? 

I mean, it definitely wasn't this bad the whole time, I promise. I really tried to be a good student and push through it at first, I didn't just give up right away. It's just been sort of a... a slow decline since then, where things just got harder and harder to do. 

Is that the kind of timeline you were looking for? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
When you're sitting in your room, what's going through your mind? Are you feeling sad or down, or are you mostly worried or anxious about things?

Um... I really want to give you a good answer, but... I hope it doesn't make me sound, I don't know, weird or broken? But I don't think I'm really feeling sad. And I'm not really anxious, either. 

I know I probably should be worried about sitting there all day, but... honestly, most of the time, my mind is just kind of... blank. I'm not really thinking about much of anything at all. It's just sort of empty and quiet. 

I'm so sorry if that's not very helpful for you to figure things out. Is it okay if I don't really have a better way to explain it? I hope I'm not making your job too difficult.

When you think about the things you used to enjoy doing, like knitting or journaling, do you feel any desire or interest in doing them again, or does the idea of doing them just not appeal to you at all anymore?

Um... I really wish I could tell you that I still want to do them. I know I probably *should* want to, and I really hope you don't think I'm just being difficult or lazy. But... yeah, the idea of doing them just doesn't really appeal to me at all right now. 

It's kind of like I was saying earlier... I mostly just can't make myself do anything anymore. I'll look at my journal or my knitting, and... I don't know, there's just no spark. No drive to pick it up. That's why I end up just sitting in my room in the same clothes all day, not going for walks or doing anything... and why I barely have the energy to answer my mom when she asks what's wrong. I just don't have it in me to care about those things right now, even the ones I used to really like. 

I'm really sorry, I know that probably sounds so bad. Is it okay that I feel that way? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of answer.
Have you ever had periods where you felt unusually energetic, upbeat, or like you needed less sleep than normal—maybe where you felt like you could do a lot of things or your thoughts were racing?

Um... no, I don't think so. I really hope I'm understanding you right, but... I've never really felt like that. 

I've never been super energetic or, you know, felt like I didn't need to sleep. I wish I had a little more energy sometimes, so I wouldn't just be sitting around, but... no, I've never had a time where my thoughts were racing or anything like that. I'm usually just... quiet. 

I hope that's okay? I know sometimes people have, like, ups and downs, but I really just have the... the empty feeling. I'm sorry if I'm not giving you the kind of symptoms you're looking for to figure this out. I'm really trying to be honest, I promise.

Before this started two years ago when you enrolled in community college, had you ever experienced a period like this before—where you felt this same emptiness, lack of energy, and loss of interest in things you normally enjoyed?

Um... no, I don't think so. I really hope I'm remembering everything right for you, but... no, before college, I was pretty... normal, I guess? 

I mean, high school was just regular high school. I'd go to class, hang out a little, do my knitting... I definitely didn't feel like this back then. This all just sort of... started happening later. 

I really hope it's okay that this is the first time I've felt this way? I know it probably makes it harder to figure out why it's happening now. I'm sorry if I can't point to anything earlier that would help you. Am I doing okay with these questions?

Since this all started two years ago when you began college, has there been any time during these two years when you felt better—like the emptiness lifted and you had more energy and interest in things again—or has it been pretty much the same the whole time?

Um... no, it's pretty much just been the same the whole time. I really wish I could say there was a time I felt better, I know that would probably be a better answer, but... it's just been this sort of flat, empty feeling ever since college started. 

I haven't really had any days where I suddenly felt like knitting again or had the energy to do much of anything. It's just been... steady, I guess? I really hope I'm not being too difficult by saying that. I know it's probably frustrating when things don't get better, and I'm really sorry if it seems like I'm not trying hard enough to snap out of it. 

Is that the right kind of answer? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need to help me.

I want to make sure I understand your history correctly. You mentioned you felt normal before college started. Since this flat, empty feeling began two years ago, have you ever had a break from it—even a few weeks or months where you felt more like yourself again—before it came back?

Um... no, I don't think there was a break. I mean, I really wish I could say there was, because I know it would probably be a better sign if I had periods where I was okay... but no, it's just been pretty continuous. 

I haven't had a time where I felt like my old self again, not even for a few weeks. It's just been this... this same sort of heaviness the whole time. I'm really sorry, I know I just said that, and I hope it's not annoying that I'm repeating myself. I'm just trying to make sure I'm answering exactly what you're asking. 

I really hope it's okay that it's been going on this long without a break? I know it probably makes it seem like I'm not making any progress. I promise I'm not trying to be difficult.
Before college started two years ago, did you ever have a time—maybe weeks or months—where you felt depressed or down, even if it was different from how you feel now?

Um... no, I really don't think I did. I mean, I might have had a bad day here or there, like if I was stressed about a test in high school, but... never for weeks or months. I definitely wasn't depressed back then. 

I hope it's okay that I don't have anything like that to tell you? I know you're trying to figure out a pattern, and I'm really sorry if me being totally fine back then makes your job harder now. I just want to be as honest as I can so I don't mess up your evaluation. Am I doing alright with answering these? I just really want to make sure I'm being a helpful patient.

Since this flat, empty feeling started two years ago with college, have you ever had another time—separate from now—where you felt this same way again, or has it been one continuous episode the whole time?

Um... no, it's just been the one continuous episode, I guess. It hasn't gone away and come back, it's just... stayed. 

I'm so sorry, I feel like I'm just giving you the exact same answer over and over again, and I really don't want to be frustrating you. I know you're asking in different ways to make sure you get the whole picture, and I really appreciate how thorough you're being. I just... I wish I had a different answer for you this time, but it's just been this one long, continuous feeling since college started. 

Is it okay that I keep saying the same thing? I promise I'm really thinking about your questions, I'm not just brushing them off. I just want to make sure I'm doing this right.
